//: SELF-CONTAINED ON PURPOSE. Every other repo in the fleet extends a shared base by absolute path; this one is public and must typecheck on a laptop that has never heard of the machine it was written on, so the options are inlined and `scripts/typecheck.js` fetches the compiler with npx rather than reading one from somewhere outside the repo. Sources run on Node 24's native type stripping, so this never emits: it only checks. erasableSyntaxOnly is what keeps a .ts file runnable without a compiler -- no enums, no namespaces, no parameter properties.
//include: server/ is the typed half. The extension is NOT checked here, and that is a bound rather than an oversight: its browser-facing files are written against the DOM and the `chrome.*` extension API, whose ambient types are npm packages (@types/chrome), and this repo's whole test suite runs with no node_modules. See docs/decisions/0012-the-typed-half-is-the-server.md. extension/errors.js and extension/log.js are pulled in anyway, because server/ imports them.
